findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever a non-empty `totpCode` is posted
findings.description: The password check at line 121 is `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`, so any non-empty `totpCode` disables password verification for the whole `authorize` call. The new backup-code branch at line 131 runs after that and never verifies the password. A request with the email, `password: ""`, `totpCode: "x"`, and a valid `backupCode` therefore logs in with no password. The code is consumed and the user is returned (lines 148–156). The existing TOTP branch already had this short-circuit, but a backup code is a static secret, so this path needs no time-bound code. The UI does not trigger this, since lost-access clears `totpCode` and still submits the real password, so it requires a crafted POST to `/api/auth/callback/credentials`. The fix is to verify the password on the credentials path whenever `user.password` is set. The external-TOTP continuation (`login.tsx` with `totpEmail`, which submits an empty password) needs an explicit server-verified signal instead of the presence of `totpCode`. Add a test that posts a valid backup code without a password and expects rejection.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.description: Codes are read at line 73, checked in memory, and written back at line 149 from that snapshot. Two concurrent logins can both pass with the same code, so single-use is not enforced. Two different codes consumed concurrently also overwrite each other. If A nulls code 1 and B, working from the same snapshot, nulls code 2, the final write restores code 1 as valid. Use a conditional update (`updateMany` where the column still equals the snapshot, retrying on zero rows) or a transaction with a row lock.

findings.title: Backup-code verification is duplicated, and the copies already diverge
findings.description: The env check, decrypt, `JSON.parse`, and `indexOf(code.replaceAll("-", ""))` sequence is repeated in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48-64`. The copies already differ: `authorize` consumes and re-encrypts, while disable does not. Error signaling also differs, using `throw` in one and `res.status` in the other. Any fix, such as the race above or the input normalization below, must be applied twice. Extract a shared helper into `packages/features/auth/lib` and call it from both.

findings.title: Backup-code input is not type-checked or normalized
findings.description: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A truthy non-string body value throws a `TypeError` and returns a 500 instead of a 400. The same assumption appears at `next-auth-options.ts:144`. There is also no trim or lowercase. Codes are lowercase hex (`setup.ts:61`), so `ABCDE-12345` or a pasted value with trailing whitespace is rejected as incorrect. `JSON.parse` of the decrypted list returns `any` and is not validated. Parse both trust boundaries with zod (`z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`) and type the decrypted list as `string[]`.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-codes step skips `onEnable` and leaves the UI inconsistent
findings.description: `onEnable` is called only from the Close button (lines 266–270). `DialogContent` is a Radix dialog that does not prevent Escape or overlay dismissal (`packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:89-104`), so Escape or an outside click calls `onOpenChange(false)`. The parent at `apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64` only toggles the modal closed. `viewer.me` is never invalidated, so the switch shows disabled while the server has 2FA enabled. The codes exist only in this modal's memory. Setup refuses once 2FA is enabled (`setup.ts:42-44`), and no endpoint retrieves or regenerates codes, so a user who dismisses before saving can only recover by disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Ignore dismissal while the step is `DisplayBackupCodes`, or route it to the same handler as Close.

findings.title: The enable modal's password reveal toggle does not work
findings.description: The field was switched from `TextField` to `PasswordField` but kept `type="password"`. In `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:35-39`, `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` after it, so the caller's `type` wins. The eye button flips its icon and tooltip, but the field never reveals. The existing toggle test (`input.test.tsx:67-83`) renders `PasswordField` without a `type` prop, so it does not catch this. Remove `type="password"` from the caller.

findings.title: An empty backup-code submission on login fails silently
findings.description: `BackupCode`'s `required` is not enforced because the login form has `noValidate` (`login.tsx:188`), and `formSchema` only validates email and password (`login.tsx:57-66`). An empty code is falsy, so `authorize` falls into the TOTP branch and throws `SecondFactorRequired` (`next-auth-options.ts:157-159`). The client sets `twoFactorRequired(true)`, which is already true, and shows no error, so nothing visibly happens. Validate the field client-side or in zod and show a message. The nested ternary at `login.tsx:221` is hard to read and could be an `if`/`else` block.

findings.title: The copy button reports success without checking the clipboard write
findings.description: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught. `showToast(..., "success")` on line 279 runs unconditionally. A rejected write (insecure context, permission denied) produces an unhandled rejection and a false success toast. Await it inside a try/catch and show an error toast on failure.

findings.title: The new authentication paths have no unit or integration tests
findings.description: A search of test and spec files for two-factor, `backupCode`, and `next-auth-options` found no tests covering the `authorize` backup branch, the backup branch in `disable.ts`, or the code generation in `setup.ts`. The only e2e coverage added is download, copy, and close (`login.2fa.e2e.ts`). Login with a backup code, single-use consumption, and disable-with-backup are TODOs (`login.2fa.e2e.ts:12`). A unit test on `authorize` would have caught the bypass above. Before this ships, cover: a valid code is accepted and consumed, a reused code is rejected, a request without a password is rejected, and missing codes return `MissingBackupCodes`.

findings.title: An e2e assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op
findings.description: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect`, so the matcher always succeeds. The FIXME added at lines 50–51 acknowledges this but leaves it in place. Assert on the checked state the way line 127 does, using `[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]` with `toBeVisible()`.

findings.title: The password reveal toggle is removed from the tab order for every password field in the app
findings.description: `tabIndex={-1}` on the reveal button in the shared `PasswordField` applies to every password input (login, signup, settings), not only the 2FA flows. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the visibility toggle (WCAG 2.1.1). The diff does not explain the change, and the existing test only exercises click. If a specific form needs it, set it there. Otherwise revert it.

findings.title: The backup-code component is named `TwoFactor`
findings.description: The default export in `BackupCode.tsx` is `function TwoFactor(...)`, copied from `TwoFactor.tsx`. Both show up under the same name in React DevTools and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`. Also, the `Label` at line 13 has no `htmlFor="backup-code"`, so the input has no accessible name.

findings.title: Unchanged duplicate Enable/Disable modals still exist under `components/security/`
findings.description: `components/security/` has its own Enable and Disable modals and a `TwoFactorAuthSection` that predate backup codes. This diff does not touch them. A grep for imports of `TwoFactorAuthSection` finds none, so the section and its modals look unused. The settings copies now diverge from them. Delete the dead copies or document which set is canonical.

findings.title: The migration timestamp sorts before an existing migration
findings.description: The timestamp `20230804153419` is earlier than the latest existing migration, `20230828094603_add_include_calendar_event`. The statement is a nullable `ADD COLUMN`, so it is safe in any order, but history is no longer chronological. Consider renaming it to a timestamp after `20230828094603` before merge.

findings.title: The encrypted column is not in the context user omit list
findings.description: `twoFactorSecret` is omitted from the context user type, but `backupCodes` is not. Runtime is safe today: `getUserFromSession` (`packages/trpc/server/middlewares/sessionMiddleware.ts:24-60`) uses an explicit `select` that does not include `backupCodes`. Add `"backupCodes"` to the `Omit` so the type stays accurate if a spread is added later.

findings.title: Backup codes are 40 bits, and the disable path has no rate limit
findings.description: `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` produces 10 hex characters, or 40 bits. `disable.ts` does not call `checkRateLimitAndThrowError`, while login does (`next-auth-options.ts:109`). The password gate on disable limits an attacker to someone who already has the password and a session, so the risk is modest. Still, a longer code, for example 16 characters, and a rate limit on the disable backup path would bring it in line with common recovery-code practice.

findings.title: Plaintext codes stay in dialog state after close, and the blob URL is never revoked on unmount
findings.description: `resetState` clears the password and error but not `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `secret`, or `dataUri`. The parent keeps this modal mounted, so plaintext codes remain in React state after close. The object URL holding the codes is revoked only on regeneration, never on unmount. Also, `useState([])` at line 64 infers `never[]`, so it should be `useState<string[]>([])`. `formatBackupCode` (line 163) is pure and belongs at module scope.

findings.title: The download link wraps a button
findings.description: `<a download>` wraps a `<Button>`, which renders a `<button>`. Interactive content nested inside an anchor is invalid HTML and exposes two controls to screen readers. Make the anchor the styled control, or use a button whose click handler triggers the download.

findings.title: Backup codes use a CSPRNG and are stored encrypted, and disable still requires the password
findings.description: `setup.ts:61` generates codes with `crypto.randomBytes`, and `setup.ts:68` stores the list with `symmetricEncrypt`, the same way the TOTP secret is stored. `disable.ts:40-45` still verifies the password for CAL accounts before any second-factor branch, so the backup-code branch does not weaken disable. The finding above about the login path is separate from this.
